scope: finite directed developmental state graphs with explicitly charged nonnegative integer transition costs, finite current/future obligation sets, and bounded descendant budgets
assumptions: developmental states and legal transitions are finite and prospectively registered
every transition cost includes the charged developmental/search work represented by that edge
current capability is evaluated before any new adaptation for the future obligation
useful-descendant mass counts descendant states/equivalence classes rather than path multiplicity
optional-inheritance monotonicity applies only when every old edge at the same cost remains feasible and inherited structure adds optional paths without mandatory maintenance or repricing
claim_boundary: This closes a bounded definitional/proof spine for seven H rows. It does not yet predict maintenance-cost reversal, representation/operator/search-prior benefits, reset regimes, expansion/pruning, self-compilation, local morphogenesis, multi-generation trajectories, or open-endedness; no G7 claim is made.
strongest_parent: weighted shortest-path/control reachability, transfer-learning sample/search complexity, evolutionary accessibility/evolvability, option-value monotonicity
negative_twin: make inherited structure mandatory or reprice/remove an old path; the free-option monotonicity theorem must refuse the instance rather than claiming inheritance cannot hurt
nearest_counterexample: with mandatory maintenance, shared-budget coupling, changed transition costs, or hidden state-dependent constraints, inherited structure may increase future burden even though a free optional extension cannot
falsifier: Any registered definition changes under pure path duplication, any shortest-path burden disagrees with exhaustive finite reachability, current capability alone identifies future learning potential in the separation witness, or a legal free optional extension increases minimum burden/decreases useful-descendant mass.

rows.ledger_row: Define current capability separately from future learning potential.
rows.definition: Current capability is success fraction on current obligations without further adaptation; future learning potential at budget B is the fraction of registered future obligations whose satisfying state set is reachable with minimum adaptation burden <= B.
rows.negative_twin: two states have the same current outputs and the same future shortest-path burdens; both quantities then coincide only accidentally
rows.falsifier: no finite witness exists with equal current capability but unequal future learning potential

rows.definition: For start state x and future obligation satisfying set G, adaptation burden A(x,G) is the minimum total charged transition cost of any legal developmental path from x into G, or infinity if G is unreachable.
rows.strongest_parent: weighted shortest path / optimal control cost-to-go
rows.negative_twin: an unreachable target has infinite rather than fabricated finite burden
rows.falsifier: computed burden differs from the minimum charged legal path cost

rows.definition: At budget B, useful-descendant mass is the sum of prospectively registered nonnegative weights of useful descendant states/equivalence classes whose minimum developmental burden from the current state is <= B; multiple paths to one descendant do not multiply its mass.
rows.negative_twin: duplicate a developmental path to an already reachable descendant; mass must not increase
rows.falsifier: mass changes under pure duplicate-path insertion or counts an unreachable-over-budget descendant

rows.definition: For a prospectively registered target morphology set M*, morphology-search burden is the minimum fully charged developmental transition/search cost from the current state to any member of M*, or infinity if unreachable.
rows.negative_twin: representable but unreachable morphology has infinite search burden
rows.falsifier: a cheaper legal fully charged path to M* exists than the reported burden

rows.ledger_row: Define transfer benefit and harmful transfer.
rows.definition: For the same future obligation G, transfer benefit is A(reset,G) - A(continued,G). Positive is beneficial transfer, zero neutral, negative harmful transfer; infinities retain their reachability meaning.
rows.negative_twin: swap reset and continued states; any finite nonzero transfer benefit changes sign
rows.falsifier: reported transfer sign disagrees with the two independently computed adaptation burdens

rows.definition: Two developmental histories are path-dependent at the registered future scope when their present observable outputs are equal but the resulting internal developmental states have unequal adaptation burden for at least one registered future obligation.
rows.negative_twin: if present outputs differ, future burden differences do not establish the intended hidden-history witness
rows.falsifier: states declared path-dependent have either unequal present outputs or identical burdens for every registered future obligation

rows.ledger_row: Prove optional inheritance monotonicity at its actual scope.
rows.definition: If inherited structure is a free optional extension: every base developmental edge remains available at exactly the same cost and inheritance only adds legal paths, then minimum adaptation/morphology burden cannot increase and useful-descendant mass at any fixed budget cannot decrease.
rows.negative_twin: replace an old unit-cost path by a mandatory higher-cost path; premise fails and burden may increase
rows.falsifier: a graph satisfying exact base-edge/cost inclusion has a target with larger inherited minimum burden or smaller inherited useful-descendant mass
